title: App conversion tornado to starlette breaks page, when logged in
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When migrating an existing app from streamlit 1.56.0 to 1.58.0 server backend is changed from tornado to starlette. When using st.user.login() cookies are stored for 30 days. When the backend now is changed, the cookies prevent the page from loading. Once the cookies are deleted or expired everything works as usual.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

if not st.user.is_logged_in:
  st.login()
else:
  print("Hello World")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

The old cookies should be deleted, if the backend is changed or tokens are invalid.

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.58.0
- Python version: 3.14.5
- Operating System: debian
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

### Triage summary

This is a regression caused by the Tornado → Starlette migration (default server change introduced in 1.57.0 via PR #14553). When upgrading from 1.56.0 to 1.58.0, the browser still holds the `_streamlit_user` / `_streamlit_user_tokens` cookies that were originally signed by Tornado's `set_signed_cookie` scheme (`max_age_days=30`). The new server signs/verifies cookies via `itsdangerous.URLSafeTimedSerializer` in `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_app_utils.py::decode_signed_value`, which uses a completely different signature format. Because the two formats are incompatible, every old cookie fails verification — but `decode_signed_value` simply swallows `BadSignature` and returns `None` (see `_get_signed_cookie_from_request` in `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_auth_routes.py`), and the invalid cookies are never cleared on the response. The browser keeps re-sending them on every request, which can leave the app stuck on the loading screen / OAuth flow until the user manually deletes the cookies or they expire after ~30 days.

The expected behavior — as the reporter notes — is that the server should clear (or treat as absent and overwrite) auth cookies it cannot validate, so an upgrade from 1.56 → ≥1.57 does not require a manual cookie purge by every previously-logged-in user.

### Related Issues

- [#15193 — Auth cookies set by `st.login()` are session-scoped in 1.57.0 (regression from 1.56)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15193): Same Tornado → Starlette cookie regression in the same code path (`_set_single_cookie`), already confirmed and fixed (restored 30-day `max_age`). Strong candidate for cross-reference / shared follow-up.
- [#14991 — OAuth MismatchingStateError regression in 1.57.0 (works in 1.56.0)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14991): Another `st.login` regression caused by the Starlette migration where stale session/cookie state from older versions interferes with the new auth flow.
- [#15115 — OAuth authentication fails during token exchange with "Invalid code verifier"](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15115): A third 1.57.0 starlette-auth regression involving cookies/state being interpreted incorrectly by the new server — useful as a pattern for "carry-over auth state breaks the new backend".

Hi [USER] and team 

I just noticed that #15420 was merged and issue #15407 has been closed as completed — congratulations on the quick turnaround!

I wasn't aware of the parallel effort when I opened this PR. I'm happy to close it to keep the repo clean.

For what it's worth, my approach introduced a dedicated `InvalidAuthCookieMiddleware` that intercepts stale cookies at the HTTP layer and also closes WebSocket connections with code 1012 before session creation, driving the frontend into its PINGING_SERVER retry loop for a self-healing reconnect. If any of those ideas are useful as a follow-up or complement to #15420, feel free to cherry-pick — otherwise no worries at all.

Thanks for maintaining such a welcoming project. Looking forward to contributing again on a fresh issue!
